title: Threshold characterization of deterministic communication complexity
statement: Let $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ be a two-argument function and let $n$ be a natural number. Then the deterministic communication complexity $D(f)$ satisfies $D(f) \le n$ if and only if there exists a deterministic communication protocol $p$ over inputs $X$ and $Y$ that computes $f$ and whose communication complexity is at most $n$.
hypotheses_covered: f is a function X → Y → α
replaced:
For $f : X \to Y \to \alpha$ and $n : \mathbb{N}$, we have $D(f) \le n$ if and only if
there exists a protocol $p : \mathrm{Protocol}\;X\;Y\;\alpha$ such that $p$ computes $f$
and $p.\mathrm{complexity} \le n$.
